title_zh: 小时级重置？Sylvia Jablonski与Justin Schacht谈盘中重置杠杆ETF
subtitle_zh: Defiance申报16只每小时重置2倍杠杆ETF，Justin Schacht解析散户激增与市场结构隐忧。

turns.en: The ETF Edge podcast is sponsored by Invesco QQQ. Let's rethink possibility. Invesco Distributors, Inc. Welcome to ETF Edge, the podcast. If you're looking to learn the latest insights on all things exchange-traded funds, you're in the right place.
turns.zh: 《ETF Edge》播客由 Invesco QQQ 赞助播出。让我们重新想象可能性。——Invesco Distributors, Inc. 欢迎收听《ETF Edge》播客。如果你想了解交易型开放式指数基金（ETF）方方面面的最新洞见，那你来对地方了。

turns.en: Every week, we're bringing you compelling interviews, thoughtful market analysis, and breaking down what it all means for investors. I'm your host, Dominic Chu.
turns.zh: 每周我们都会为你带来精彩的访谈、有深度的市场分析，并拆解这一切对投资者意味着什么。我是你的主持人 Dominic Chu。

turns.en: Retail investors' demand for new products is pushing issuers to get sharper and sharper with their new offerings. In more ways than one. And that could cut both ways.
turns.zh: 散户对新产品旺盛的需求，正逼着发行商把新品做得越来越锋利，而且不止一个维度。这可能是一把双刃剑。

turns.en: Here's my conversation with Sylvia Jablonski, the CIO and co-founder at Defiance ETFs, and Justin Schacht, Rosenblatt Security's partner and head of market structure.
turns.zh: 以下是我与 Defiance ETFs 首席投资官兼联合创始人 Sylvia Jablonski，以及 Rosenblatt Securities 合伙人兼市场结构研究主管 Justin Schacht 的对谈。

turns.en: I wanna start, first of all, with some of the news, I guess, that's coming out in this, and the reason why we're talking about this. And it's for you, Sylvia.
turns.zh: 我想先聊聊最近传出的相关消息，也就是我们今天为什么谈这个话题。Sylvia，这个问题先抛给你。

turns.en: We know that there is now a filing that has been made, and we are gonna see at some point, if the regulators kind of let this thing go and come to fruition, a more, I guess, robust offering of inverse and levered type products, but not just reset on a daily basis, reset on an intraday basis, and in some cases, on the hourly basis.
turns.zh: 我们知道现在已经有申报提交上去了，如果监管机构放行、让它最终落地，我们早晚可能会看到更丰富的一批反向（inverse）和杠杆（leveraged）类产品——不只是每日重置，而是盘中重置，有些甚至是按小时重置。

turns.en: Can you take us through, Sylvia, why you and your firm are one of the people that spearheading this movement towards more specified tools in ETF markets?
turns.zh: Sylvia，能不能请你带我们了解一下，为什么你和你的公司会是ETF市场这股更精细化工具潮流的推动者之一？

turns.en: Yes, and good afternoon, Dom, and I'm glad that we're the one making the noise in the ETF industry. That's always good to hear. Hopefully it's good noise, but yeah.
turns.zh: 好的，下午好，Dom。很高兴是我们成了ETF行业里制造声量的那一家，这总归是好事情。希望是好名声吧。

turns.en: So Defiance has filed for 16 hourly reset leveraged ETFs, and so there are two times levered funds, similar to the two ex-daily funds that are out there, but instead of resetting at the end of the trading day, they reset at the end of each hour.
turns.zh: Defiance 申报了16只小时级重置杠杆ETF，都是2倍杠杆（2x）基金，和市面上已有的2倍每日基金类似，只不过它们不是在收盘时重置，而是在每个小时结束时重置。

turns.en: So you'll have six resets or so per day, they reset hourly, and so why do this? The reason why is because for the last decades or so, Defiance has just been watching levered and inverse traders and monitoring their behaviors and kind of looking at the holding periods, and what was notable to us is that the two ex-daily funds are sometimes held for periods of time that are shorter than one day, and why is that?
turns.zh: 也就是说每天大约重置六次、每小时都重置。为什么要这么做？原因是过去几十年里，Defiance 一直在观察杠杆和反向产品的交易者，监测他们的行为、研究持有周期。让我们印象深刻的是，这些2倍每日基金有时候持有时间不足一天，为什么会这样？

turns.en: That's because I think active and sophisticated traders are looking to trade on news. They're looking to trade on a tweet, they're looking to trade on an earnings call, a drug discovery announcement.
turns.zh: 因为我认为活跃且成熟的交易员是想围绕新闻来交易。他们想对一条推文交易，对一次财报电话会交易，对一个药物研发公告交易。

turns.en: You kind of saw that happen with Moderna the other day, and there's no product out there that actually captures the compounding hour to hour or for that hour, and so we really thought that there was a room for this in the market.
turns.zh: 前几天 Moderna 的情况你大概也看到了，而现在没有任何产品能真正捕捉小时级的复利效应、或者说某一个小时内的行情。所以我们真心觉得市场在这个方向上有空间。

turns.en: We thought it was a precise tool for those hourly traders, which very much are out there in the market and exist, and we're doing the top names, like the NVIDIA, Tesla, Meta, Microsoft, we filed for 16 November or so, and it's just for these traders looking for that precise exposure.
turns.zh: 我们认为这是为按小时交易的投资者打造的精准工具，这类投资者在市场上实实在在地存在。我们做的是头部标的，比如 NVIDIA、Tesla、Meta、Microsoft，我们在11月前后申报了这16只产品，就是为这些寻找精准敞口的交易员准备的。

turns.en: That precise exposure, if I could just follow up Sylvia, have you seen, and you've obviously done a lot of research and market analysis on the types of traders, the types of people who use these products, just how much demand do you think there will be for these types of products that don't just reset on a daily basis, because it was already tough enough to have some investors and traders risk manage around that,
turns.zh: 说到这种精准敞口，Sylvia，我想追问一下。你在研究交易员类型、使用这些产品的人群方面显然做了大量工作——你觉得这种不按日重置的产品需求到底会有多大？因为光围绕每日重置做好风险管理就已经让一些投资者和交易员够头疼了，

turns.en: but now have to do it on an intraday basis, possibly six times a day. Right, so if you look at the, kind of the TAM of the levered ETFs, I mean, they've massively grown 31% of all ETF launches this year were levered and inverse funds.
turns.zh: 现在还得在盘中做，一天可能要六次。是的，如果你看一下杠杆ETF的总可市场规模（TAM），它已经大幅膨胀——今年所有新发ETF里有31%是杠杆和反向基金。

turns.en: You're talking about hundreds of billions that have come into the space globally, and so we think that very much, it's in that neighborhood, right?
turns.zh: 全球流入这个领域的资金已经是数千亿美元量级，所以我们判断需求就在这个量级附近。

turns.en: So any trader that is looking to trade a daily levered product that resets at the end of the day, could be interested in trading it for an hour.
turns.zh: 所以任何一个本来想交易每日收盘重置的杠杆产品的交易员，都可能愿意以一小时为维度去交易。

turns.en: We're not saying that every trader's going to come in and hold it for the six hour period. Some may trade it for an hour, some may hold it for the six hour period.
turns.zh: 我们并不是说每个交易员都会进来持有满六个小时。有人可能只交易一个小时，有人可能持有满六个小时。

turns.en: It depends on the direction of the market, the type of momentum that they're getting during the day. It's the same type of thing, right? When you have a bull fund and the market is rising, compounding works in your favor over a period of time.
turns.zh: 这取决于市场方向、盘中他们感受到的动量类型。道理是一样的：当你持有看涨（bull）基金而市场一路上行，复利效应在一段时间里会对你有利。

turns.en: Well, if you have a bull market and the prices are rising throughout the day, compounding works in your favor potentially more so than a levered ETF that rebalances at the end of the day.
turns.zh: 而且如果是牛市、价格全天都在上涨，复利带来的优势甚至可能超过只在收盘时再平衡的杠杆ETF。

turns.en: I want to mitigate that and say that these are still levered funds in volatile range bound markets. You can certainly decay, lose profits and things like this.
turns.zh: 但我也要稍微降降温：这些终究还是杠杆基金。在震荡、区间波动的市场里，你当然会遭遇损耗（decay）、利润回吐，诸如此类。

turns.en: They're for sophisticated traders, but that's the intention. To really take advantage of that intraday compounding. All right, that's good context to put it in because then Justin, I will turn to you about this.
turns.zh: 它们是给成熟交易员准备的，但初衷就是真正利用盘中的复利效应。好的，这个背景很清楚了。Justin，这部分我想转到你这边。

turns.en: As somebody who has watched market structure now for decades at this point, you've seen a lot of different products come to market and you've seen a lot of different ripple effects happen because of those product launches.
turns.zh: 作为研究市场结构几十年的资深人士，你见过太多产品上市，也见过这些产品发行引发的种种连锁反应。

turns.en: What do you think about intraday reset, levered and or inverse type ETFs? Do you think that there's going to be a market impact for those people who trade it?
turns.zh: 你怎么看盘中重置的杠杆或反向ETF？你觉得对交易它们的人来说，会产生市场影响吗？

turns.en: Or is it going to be somewhat of a runway because it won't be highly adopted right in the beginning but could see a little bit more of that evolution as the weeks and quarters go by?
turns.zh: 还是说它更像一条跑道——一开始不会被大规模采用，但随着几周、几个季度过去，会看到更多演变？

turns.en: I mean, that's really an unknown, unknown dom. I'd love to be able to have a better answer for you on what the future will hold for that. I can tell you that the products that exist today, dovetailing on some of the things that Silvia brought up are very, very popular.
turns.zh: 这真的是一个未知数，Dom。我也希望能给你一个更好的答案。但我可以告诉你，今天已经存在的那些产品——顺着 Sylvia 提到的几点说——已经非常非常受欢迎了。

turns.en: When we look at, you know, we put out a report every month on ETP activity in the marketplace. And I think just today we set out the most recent version.
turns.zh: 我们每月都会发布一份交易所交易产品（ETP）市场活跃度的报告，我想就在今天刚发布了最新版本。

turns.en: We looked at the month of August. And I think it was eight of the top 10 ETFs by volume. Average daily volume were leveraged and inverse products.
turns.zh: 我们看了8月的数据，按日均成交量排的前10名ETF里，我记得有8只是杠杆和反向产品。

turns.en: And even if you looked at just the entire stock market, four of the top 10 equities period, including corporates and ETFs were single stock, you know, ultra long, ultra short type products.
turns.zh: 哪怕把整个股票市场放在一起看——个股和ETF都算——成交量前10名里也有4只是单只个股的极端做多、极端做空类产品。

turns.en: Now, the markets are very interconnected, right? So someone owning or Silvia's firm operating this is gonna have to figure out a way to provide that exposure in the underlying name.
turns.zh: 当然，市场是高度互联的。无论是持有这类产品的人，还是像 Sylvia 的公司这样运作它的发行商，都必须想办法在底层标的上提供相应的敞口。

turns.en: So, I mean, she'll be much better positioned to explain how that happens than I will. But then you also have people that make markets in these instruments.
turns.zh: 具体怎么实现，她肯定比我更有资格解释。但除此之外，还有人为这些品种做市。

turns.en: So while they're buying and selling that instrument, they also tend to be buying and selling the underlying stock, maybe the options that are based on that product, maybe index options that those stocks are a part of.
turns.zh: 所以他们在买卖这些产品的同时，往往也在买卖底层股票、可能还有以该产品为标的的期权、这些股票所在指数的指数期权。

turns.en: And so, you know, there is the potential for movements in one security to affect other securities and the broader market. I will say that as I think about when you're talking about maybe some of the ripple effects, the market has evolved in ways over the past 10 to 15 years that provide some safeguards there.
turns.zh: 所以确实存在这种可能：一个证券的波动会波及其他证券和更广泛的市场。不过说到你提到的那些连锁反应，我想指出，过去10到15年间市场的演化已经提供了一些保障。

turns.en: So some people may remember the flash crash of May, 2010. We now have intraday volatility protections in the form of something called limit up, limit down bands.
turns.zh: 有些人可能记得2010年5月的闪崩（flash crash）。我们现在有了盘中波动保护机制，也就是所谓的涨跌限制带（limit up, limit down bands）。

turns.en: So if something happens to really go down or up by a tremendous amount in a short period of time, that security can get halted. So we have a way to make sure that if everybody is heading for the exits or rushing into the entrance at one time, that that can happen in a more orderly fashion.
turns.zh: 所以如果某个证券在短时间内暴涨暴跌，它会被临时停牌。这样即使所有人都同时夺门而逃或一拥而入，交易也能更有序地进行。

turns.en: Justin, can I follow up there by speaking a little bit more to that dynamic vis-a-vis the regulatory environment that we're in right now? A lot has been made about this current iteration of regulators both at the SEC, the CFTC, and elsewhere in the financial markets that seem to be a little bit more if you'll kind of forgive the generalization of it, more open towards product innovation and towards kind of letting these products develop
turns.zh: Justin，我可以顺着这里再追问一点，把这种动态和我们当下的监管环境联系起来吗？现在大家都在谈论这一轮监管机构——SEC、CFTC以及金融市场的其他监管方——如果允许我做这种概括的话，似乎对产品创新更开放，更愿意让这些产品先发展起来，

turns.en: and kind of seeing how they work in the wild, so to speak, before they really try to kind of limit their dynamics and whatnot. How much does that regulatory environment factor in to how much somebody like you has to figure out how these instruments will ultimately ripple through market structure?
turns.zh: 先看看它们在“野外”实际怎么运行，然后再去限制它们的动能等等。这样的监管环境，对你这样需要预判这些工具最终如何冲击市场结构的人，影响有多大？

turns.en: Yeah, I mean, we tend to be reactive, right? So when we see, I think you're absolutely right, we are in an environment where the folks in Washington tend to be more permissive, they tend to be more hands-off, free market oriented and say, you know, look, as long as the customer understands and there was disclosure and they know what they're getting into, we're not going to try to be the nanny state and say,
turns.zh: 嗯，我们更像是被动响应的一方。你说得完全没错，现在华盛顿的监管者整体更宽容、更不干预、更偏向自由市场，他们的态度是：只要客户看得懂、有信息披露、知道自己进场是干什么的，我们就不去当保姆国家，不会说

turns.en: well, this is what you should be trading or shouldn't be trading. You know, they're not about to say you should just be like Jack Bogle, right?
turns.zh: 你该交易这个、不该交易那个。他们不会站出来说“你就该学 Jack Bogle 那样”，对吧？

turns.en: You know, they're going to say, go ahead and experiment with these things, as long as you know what you're getting into and what the risks are.
turns.zh: 他们会说的是：去尝试、去实验吧，只要你知道自己在做什么、风险是什么。

turns.en: For us, we just sort of watch what happens and as these products come out and more and more trading goes into them, that affects a lot of the dynamics that we look at for our institutional customers, for instance.
turns.zh: 对我们来说就是观察事态发展。随着这些产品推出、越来越多的交易量涌进去，它会影响到我们为机构客户关注的很多市场动态。

turns.en: What percentage of the market is coming from retail, of the volume in the market is coming from retail because we have institutional customers that are trying to figure out, well, when I'm buying and selling or selling XYZ stock, how much of that liquidity in the market is actually accessible to me?
turns.zh: 比如市场成交量里有多大比例来自散户，因为机构客户一直在琢磨：当我买入或卖出 XYZ 股票时，市场上到底有多少流动性是我真正能用得上的？

turns.en: Because retail volume tends to just sort of get siphoned off and executed off exchange where they can't interact with it. So we look at things like that very, very closely.
turns.zh: 因为散户的成交量往往被虹吸到场外（off-exchange）成交，机构无法与之撮合。所以这类问题我们盯得非常紧。

turns.en: As these products get more popular, they account for a larger and larger percentage of the volume in the marketplace. Sylvia, how much has that regulatory environment factored into what you're doing over at Defiance, what other people in the business the industry are doing with regard to putting out new product?
turns.zh: 随着这些产品越来越受欢迎，它们在市场成交中的占比也越来越大。Sylvia，当前的监管环境在多大程度上影响了你们 Defiance 正在做的事，以及行业内其他人推新产品的动作？

turns.en: You mentioned, and you and Justin both, some of the stats around the growth of actively managed ETFs, those that use leverage, those that use kind of the inverse nature of performance.
turns.zh: 你和 Justin 都提到了一些数据，关于主动管理ETF的增长、使用杠杆的产品、以及反向业绩类产品的数据。

turns.en: How much do you kind of think about the market dynamic and how much do you think about demand, that total addressable market, before you conceive of some of these types of products and then seek the regulatory approval to bring them to market?
turns.zh: 在构思这些产品、再去寻求监管批准推向市场之前，你们对市场动态思考多少？对需求、对总可市场规模思考多少？

turns.en: Well, I think this has probably been one of the most exciting years or the last two years, in particular, in ETFs that I've ever seen in my ETF career anyway.
turns.zh: 我觉得这可能是我ETF职业生涯里见过的最令人兴奋的时候之一，尤其是过去两年。

turns.en: You're talking about $16.4 trillion worth of ETFs and close to 300 billion of thematics in 2026. The amount of funds that have launched so far this year is over 1,000 and that was the, I think there were about 1,100 that launched the entire year last year, right?
turns.zh: 现在讲的是16.4万亿美元的ETF规模，以及2026年接近3000亿美元的主题类ETF。今年到目前为止新发的基金已经超过1000只——我记得去年全年大概发了1100只左右，对吧？

turns.en: So we're at like a 50% increase there. What's changed in ETFs? So to answer your question, how much do we think about it? We know the appetite is there because we've seen it in our own products, especially around AI and anything that has to do with AI, AI infrastructure and its cousins, like the quantum, the AI power, the capacitors, all of these different themes have taken off very, very quickly.
turns.zh: 相当于增长了大约50%。ETF到底变了什么？回答你的问题：我们想了多少？我们知道需求是存在的，因为在我们自己的产品上就看到过，尤其围绕AI、和AI沾边的一切——AI基础设施和它的表亲：量子、AI电力、电容器，所有这些主题都起飞得飞快。

turns.en: It used to be that you come out with a thematic ETF idea, you spend a whole lot of time trying to get out there and educate and market the product and teach about the theme.
turns.zh: 过去你有一个主题ETF的想法，要花大量时间跑到市场上做教育、推产品、讲这个主题。

turns.en: But ETFs have been moving so quickly now that in the blink of an eye, some of these products become so popular because they didn't exist and the market appetite is insatiable for some of these AI related themes.
turns.zh: 但现在ETF的节奏快得惊人，一眨眼的功夫，有些产品就会火起来——因为之前根本不存在，而市场对AI相关主题的胃口是无止境的。

turns.en: And so what's changed now, I would say, is not so much the regulatory environment. We have all of the same processes and procedures. We have to follow all of the same rules and seek all of the same permissions to go effective.
turns.zh: 所以要说现在变了什么，我觉得不是监管环境。我们还是走同样的流程、同样的程序，要遵守同样的规则、寻求同样的批准才能生效。

turns.en: And it's kind of the regulators bless funds to go effective and can stop funds and everything remains the same. What I will say that has changed is that if you have a good idea as an ETF issuer, you have to move so quickly because products are coming to filing so quickly and the competition is just so hot for the same theme amongst us issuer.
turns.zh: 监管机构批准基金生效、也可以叫停基金，一切都还是老样子。但确实变了的一点是：作为ETF发行商，如果你有个好点子，就必须动作极快，因为产品涌向申报的速度太快了，同一主题在我们发行商之间的竞争极其白热化。

turns.en: So it's really like who has the most disruptive idea, can get it to be filed in the quickest amount of time and obviously construct the right way and think through it.
turns.zh: 所以现在比的是：谁拥有最具颠覆性的点子、谁能最快完成申报，当然还要用正确的方式把它构建好、想透。

turns.en: It's just become highly competitive, I would say. Sylvia, how much is that first mover advantage, something that you have to pay attention to as an ETF provider, a sponsor of some of these funds?
turns.zh: 可以说竞争已经高度白热化了。Sylvia，作为ETF提供商、这些基金的发起人，先发优势是你们必须重视的东西吗？

turns.en: You mentioned the competitive nature of everything that's going on. Is it maybe the assertion that you have that if you are not maybe first or second to market for some of these new hot products that you don't have as much of an edge or can't make it a viable business, at least for some of these funds going forward, if you're not kind of first or second out of the block?
turns.zh: 你提到现在一切都在拼竞争。你的判断是不是：对这些新的热门产品，如果你不是第一或第二个上市的，优势就没那么大，至少对其中一些基金而言，以后很难做成一门有前途的生意——除非你抢在起跑线的第一第二？

turns.en: Yeah, I mean, we have seen that time and time again and we have been bitten by that at defiance, right? So you definitely, if you have an idea and you have high conviction as an ETF issuer, you want to be first to market, you have the best chance of success, particularly for thematic funds.
turns.zh: 是的，我们一次又一次看到这一点，Defiance 自己也被这一点咬过。所以作为ETF发行商，如果你有想法、有强信念，你一定要抢首发上市，成功的概率才最大，主题基金尤其如此。

turns.en: I think with leveraged funds, you've seen that in the case of SpaceX. There are several leveraged SpaceX funds, a lot of issuers gathered assets there and are doing well, but there aren't so many examples of that.
turns.zh: 我想杠杆基金里 SpaceX 算一个例子。现在有好几只 SpaceX 相关的杠杆基金，很多发行商在那里聚拢了资产、做得不错，但这样的例子并不多。

turns.en: It's usually there's a winner and a loser and with thematic ETFs, you've really seen that play out and so first mover advantage just goes such a long way.
turns.zh: 通常是一赢家一输家，主题ETF里这一点体现得淋漓尽致，所以先发优势真的能决定很长一段路。

turns.en: All right, so first mover, Justin, to your side of things, how much do you pay attention to these new types of products coming to market, specifically in this case here with intraday resets for levered and or inverse type products coming out in the future?
turns.zh: 好，说到先发优势，Justin，从你那边看，你对这些新类型产品上市关注多少？特别是未来盘中重置的杠杆或反向产品。

turns.en: How much do you kind of have to factor in what you know and don't know into how you will analyze the impact of some of these types of products for your clients?
turns.zh: 在为你的客户分析这类产品的冲击时，你必须把哪些已知和未知的因素纳入考量？

turns.en: In other words, what types of things will you be looking at from a variable basis and or information databases to kind of give you the ammunition you need to provide the most insights to your clients over at Rosenblatt?
turns.zh: 换句话说，你会从哪些变量、哪些信息库里找东西，为 Rosenblatt 的客户提供最有价值的洞察弹药？

turns.en: How exactly do you add value knowing the types of products that are coming out are getting even more sophisticated like they are right now? Yeah, well, it's not so much the focus on the ETF itself for us because they tend to be more retail oriented products and not institutional products, but how they impact the underlying and so that would be the individual stocks on which they're based, but also just the broader market
turns.zh: 产品越来越复杂，你们到底怎么增值？嗯，对我们来说，重点其实不在ETF本身，因为它们更偏散户导向，不是机构产品；我们看的是它们对底层的影响——包括其挂钩的单只股票，也包括整体市场。

turns.en: and if we're trading say 15 billion or 20 billion shares a day, which seems like a crazy number now when we were at 6 billion not that long ago, how much of that is just from this retail activity in instruments like these and then the activity that they generate in the underlying and some of the other related instruments in the market.
turns.zh: 以及如果现在每天成交150亿或200亿股——不久前还只有60亿股，这数字听着都疯狂——其中有多少就来自散户在这些工具上的交易，以及它们在底层和其他相关品种上带动的活动？

turns.en: So if somebody is trading one of those underlying stocks as part of an institutional portfolio, someone sitting on the trading desk really wants to know like, okay, what is the addressable liquidity available to me?
turns.zh: 所以如果有人代表机构组合去交易其中一只底层股票，坐在交易台上的人就非常想知道：我实际可用的可触及流动性到底有多少？

turns.en: And in most cases, the retail trading is not available for them to interact with. So they're always trying to make this calibration of, okay, the volume is X in this name, I have to do a haircut on that so I can know what the liquidity is, I can know what type of execution strategy I want to pursue and then there's just also a larger sense of how involved is retail in this market and that's something that we've watched very, very closely
turns.zh: 而大多数情况下，散户的那部分交易他们是没法与之互动的。所以他们要不断做这种校准：这只股票成交量是X，我得打个折扣，才知道真实流动性、才知道该采用什么执行策略。更大层面还有散户在这个市场的参与深度，这一点我们也观察得非常仔细。

turns.en: and we've been surprised by the persistence of the demand and the retail participation. I mean, I think back to like the first wave of online brokerage in the late 90s and early aughts and the dot com craze and when that bubble burst, a lot of those people had opened up E-Trade and Ameritrade accounts when those companies were brand new, kind of closed them up and didn't come back for a long time, if ever.
turns.zh: 散户需求和参与的持久性让我们惊讶。回想90年代末、21世纪初第一波网络券商、互联网热潮，泡沫破裂时，很多在 E-Trade、Ameritrade 刚成立时就开户的人，关户离场，很久不再回来，甚至再也没有回来。

turns.en: That hasn't happened this time around. We see a generation of traders, mostly younger, that look at these sorts of instruments, they want to take higher risks with their finances, maybe than people from our generation did and they're turning to these type of products, but not only these products in the equities markets, but a whole host of other risky instruments, whether it's sports books, prediction markets,
turns.zh: 这一轮并没有重演。我们看到一代以年轻人为主的交易员，看着这类工具，愿意在财务上承担比我们这代人更高的风险。他们转向这些产品——而且不只是股票市场的这类产品，还有一大堆其他高风险工具：体育博彩、预测市场（prediction markets）、

turns.en: perpetual futures and so I think it was 20% of total stock market volume if we go back to 2020, was from retail. The data that we used to make that estimate only go back to 2020.
turns.zh: 永续期货（perpetual futures）等等。回到2020年，整个股票市场大约20%的成交量来自散户。我们做估算用的数据也只能回溯到2020年。

turns.en: I think if we went back a little bit further, it would have been even lower and the pandemic obviously was a big catalyst there. We saw that go as high as 45% in 2021.
turns.zh: 如果再往前一些，比例应该更低。疫情显然是个大催化剂，我们看到这个数字在2021年一度高达45%。

turns.en: It backed off in 2022, but it hasn't gone back down to or below 20. We're in a range of 25 to 35% now of all volume in the stock market coming from retail and I think a big reason for that is this different environment that we're in now where people feel like they need to take these risks to sort of get ahead or try to get ahead in a world where it's increasingly difficult to afford things.
turns.zh: 2022年有所回落，但再也没回到20%或以下。现在整个股票市场成交量里散户占25%到35%的区间。我觉得一个很大的原因是环境不同了：在一个很多东西越来越买不起的世界里，人们觉得必须承担这些风险才能往前赶。

turns.en: Sylvia, that leads me to my next question. The final ones, we kind of cap things off here. As you look at the universe that you have and the retail traders that traffic in your types of products over at Defiance, is it safe to say that to Justin's point, since 2020, since the pandemic and the emergence from it, that these retail traders and investors are more sophisticated.
turns.zh: Sylvia，这正好引出我的下一个问题——也是最后一个，我们收尾了。顺着 Justin 的这点，看看你们 Defiance 的产品宇宙和交易你们产品的散户，能不能这么说：自2020年、自疫情和走出疫情以来，这些散户交易者和投资者更成熟了，

turns.en: They understand the risks better in the marketplace and are better equipped to use the types of products that are being put out there right now like intraday reset levered into ETFs.
turns.zh: 对市场里的风险理解更深了，也更有能力驾驭现在推出来的这类产品，比如盘中重置的杠杆ETF？

turns.en: Yeah, absolutely. And Justin made a lot of great points and gave us a lot of good data there. I think that what happened during the pandemic is that a lot of, there were always sophisticated traders in the market that were trading 2x levered funds, whether they were retail, hedge funds or institutional, but I think what happened during the pandemic is that a lot of people were at home and for the first time became interested in trading.
turns.zh: 完全没错。Justin 刚才讲了很多很好的点，也给了很多好数据。我觉得疫情期间的情况是：市场里一直有成熟交易者在交易2倍杠杆基金——不管是散户、对冲基金还是机构——但疫情期间很多人待在家里，第一次对交易产生了兴趣。

turns.en: They became interested in how to outperform some of the types of returns that they were seeing, just having passive allocations, and for example, 401k fund.
turns.zh: 他们开始琢磨如何跑赢自己看到的那类回报——那种只做被动配置、比如放在401(k)基金里的回报。

turns.en: And some of them were younger and looking to perhaps add different types of tech and higher beta plays and slightly more risk and diversification to their portfolios.
turns.zh: 其中有些人更年轻，想在组合里加入不同类型的科技股、高beta机会，多一点风险、多一点分散。

turns.en: And they learned how to trade, they learned about markets. And I think this coupled with the amount of information out there, whether it's through all of you at CNBC educating traders and the retail community on stocks and markets and things like this, whether it's through YouTube and X and a lot of the spaces that are out there now that are really catered towards that next gen trader, there's just so much awesome education out there.
turns.zh: 他们学会了交易，学会了认识市场。再加上现在信息量这么大——无论是你们CNBC这些人在教育交易者和散户群体关于股票和市场，还是YouTube、X，以及现在很多为下一代交易者打造的空间——市面上真的有太多精彩的教育内容。

turns.en: And then what I will say is, as ETF issuers, particularly on the levered inverse stuff, the tradable 2x products and things like this, we feel such a responsibility to educate, right?
turns.zh: 我还要说一点：作为ETF发行商，尤其做杠杆反向这类可交易的2倍产品，我们深感自己有教育市场的责任。

turns.en: We don't ever go out there and try to pitch these products. We try to really educate and put it out there and explain how they work and get people comfortable with them and our competitors do the same thing to their credit.
turns.zh: 我们从来不直接推销这些产品。我们努力做真正的教育，讲清楚它们如何运作，让大家心里有数。公平地说，我们的竞争对手也在做同样的事。

turns.en: And I think that this, in the spirit of just education information that has been put out there, retail has also really learned about these products.
turns.zh: 我想在这种教育氛围和这些公开信息的推动下，散户也真的把这些产品学明白了。

turns.en: And for some retail traders, they've really benefited from that and they've embraced the singles, the levered funds, the index funds and great.
turns.zh: 对一些散户交易员来说，他们确实从中受益，积极拥抱个股（single-stock）产品、杠杆基金、指数基金，很好。

turns.en: And for others, they've realized this isn't for me and they've moved on. But I think education is a lot better. Information is very much out there in a way that it's never been before.
turns.zh: 对另一些人来说，他们意识到这不适合我，然后走开了。但我觉得教育水平好太多了，信息的普及是前所未有地充分。

turns.en: And it's really a sweet spot to be in ETFs. It's this great rapper now that actually serves its purpose when you think about what's going on in the world.
turns.zh: 现在做ETF真的正处在一个甜蜜点上。想想世界上正在发生什么，它这个封装外壳（wrapper）是真正发挥了应有作用的。

turns.en: Again, with AI and some of these derivatives of AI, it's a way to get diversified exposure to a sector that you can't trade yourself. And then the other thing I'll say is that, in recent years, it's really been the retail money that's the smart money.
turns.zh: 比如AI和AI的这些衍生主题，它是让你对无法自己直接交易的行业获得分散化敞口的一种方式。我还要说：这些年，真正的聪明钱其实是散户的钱。

turns.en: Now the institution wanna know what the retail trader is doing and kind of following their lead. So it's certainly stepped up, stepped up the knowledge in the marketplace.
turns.zh: 现在机构反而想知道散户在做什么、跟着他们的脚步走。所以市场里的认知水平确实是上了一个台阶。

turns.en: All right, so Justin, I'll give the last word to you. From your perspective and your opinion, what are the types of things that you will be looking for in the coming weeks and quarters to tell you whether or not there is any kind of a significant impact towards rolling out products that are geared towards intraday reset liquidity?
turns.zh: 好，Justin，最后的话留给你。从你的角度和判断，未来几周、几个季度，你会关注哪些信号，来判断推出这些盘中重置产品是否会产生显著影响？

turns.en: I mean, one of the easiest things to look at is just the volumes, right? Is these products, if they do get approved, they're made available to everybody.
turns.zh: 最简单的就是看成交量。这些产品一旦获批，就是向所有人开放的。

turns.en: Sylvia talks about education and that's fantastic, but it's not just the people who are receiving the education who have the ability to trade these products, right?
turns.zh: Sylvia 提到做教育，这很好，但能交易这些产品的不只是接受过教育的那批人，对吧？

turns.en: So we will look at volume, but I think over a much longer period of time, not just weeks quarters, I'll be looking to see how do people do with not just products like these, but how does that retail investor that came in in 2019 and 2020 and stuck with things, stuck with a really, you know, past a really tough 2022 and is still really engaged as they embrace these really risky products, how are they doing, right?
turns.zh: 所以我们当然会看成交量，但我觉得要看得更长，不只是几周、几个季度——我想看的是：人们用这些产品到底做得怎么样？那些2019、2020年进场、一路坚持、熬过非常艰难的2022年、到现在还在热情拥抱这些高风险产品的散户，他们过得怎么样？

turns.en: Because a lot of this stuff, you know, some people may do well with them, the ones who receive the education and focus on that may do well with them, some of them may not.
turns.zh: 因为这类东西，有人可能做得不错——那些受过教育、认真研究的人可能做得不错——但有些人可能恰恰相反。

turns.en: And I think with a lot of these risky products, particularly when you think about some of the more exotic stuff, like sports books and prediction markets, which are basically sports books and a different regulatory wrapper, the house tends to always win, right?
turns.zh: 我觉得很多这类高风险产品，尤其是更奇特的东西——像体育博彩、预测市场，后者本质上就是换了个监管外壳的博彩——庄家总是赢家，对吧？

turns.en: So I wonder if some of these folks will regret getting involved with some of these products and then maybe we'll see that retail participation decline or just the problem that is feeding this, helping feed this retail participation maybe get a little bit worse that people feel like, okay, that I tried all this risky stuff, it didn't work, now what do I do?
turns.zh: 所以我会想，这些人里会不会有人后悔参与了这些产品，然后散户参与度可能会下降；又或者是催生这种散户参与的那个问题本身变得更糟——人们觉得：我试了这么多高风险的东西，没用，那我现在该怎么办？

turns.en: Now it's time to round out the conversation with some thoughtful analysis and perspective to help you better understand ETFs with our Markets 102 portion of the podcast.
turns.zh: 接下来，用我们节目的“市场102（Markets 102）”环节给这场对话收尾，带来一些有深度的分析和视角，帮你更好地理解ETF。

turns.en: Sylvia Jablonski, the chief investment officer and co-founder at Defiance ETFs continues with us now. Sylvia, thanks for taking the time to join us on the podcast.
turns.zh: Defiance ETFs 首席投资官兼联合创始人 Sylvia Jablonski 继续留在节目里。Sylvia，感谢你抽时间参加我们的播客。

turns.en: I'm gonna start kind of along the lines of something we did talk about during the show and that was the thought process behind bringing to market a product, a possible product at this point that will give intraday reset performance on some of these kind of 2X ETFs tied to specific stocks and or baskets in the marketplace and what exactly you and the team at Defiance did in terms of conversation to come up with the idea
turns.zh: 我想先从节目中谈过的一个话题接着往下：这款产品——目前还只是潜在产品——推向市场背后的思考过程，它给挂钩特定股票或篮子的2倍ETF提供盘中重置的业绩。你和 Defiance 的团队到底经过怎样的讨论，才想出了这个点子——

turns.en: of having not just a daily reset, levered and or inverse ETF, but having one that can reset multiple times during the course of any trading day.
turns.zh: 不仅做每日重置的杠杆或反向ETF，而是做一天之内可以重置多次的ETF。

turns.en: Yeah, well, thank you again for having me here, Dom. There was a lot of conversation around this and it's just been, it's something that our clients have talked to us about, institutional sophisticated investors have talked to us about and the idea here is that, so we followed for 16 hourly reset, two times leveraged ETFs on some stocks like Nvidia, Tesla, Microsoft, things like that and some indices, things like this.
turns.zh: 嗯，Dom，再次感谢邀请。围绕这个确实讨论了很多。我们的客户——那些成熟的机构投资者——一直跟我们谈过这类需求，核心想法是这样的：我们申报了16只小时级重置2倍杠杆ETF，标的有 Nvidia、Tesla、Microsoft 这类个股，也有一些指数。

turns.en: So instead of resetting the 2X target once a day at the close, these basically reset every hour, so six or so times during the trading day and why we did this is we talked to so many of our largest traders of the 2XDLE funds and they've said, we love the 2XDLE ETFs, but markets move on such a short term.
turns.zh: 所以这些产品不再是在收盘时把2倍目标重置一次，而是每小时重置，一个交易日大约六次。我们为什么这么做？因为我们和2倍每日基金里最大的一批交易员都聊过，他们说：我们很喜欢2倍每日ETF，但市场的波动是极短期的。

turns.en: Now there's so many sharp catalysts, there's an earnings headline, there's a Fed announcement, there's a viral tweet and sometimes the day's trend or the momentum for the day happens in the course of an hour or two hours or three hours and not beyond the trading day, meaning like we see this with earnings all the time, right?
turns.zh: 现在有太多短促的催化剂：一条财报头条、一个美联储公告、一条刷屏的推文。有时候全天的趋势或动能，就发生在一两个小时、三个小时之内，出了这个窗口就没了。财报行情我们天天看到这种情形，对吧？

turns.en: Like a stock might rip at the market open and kind of stay there for a couple of hours or two and then by the end of the trading day, it's kind of back to somewhere, reverse to some kind of a bean, right?
turns.zh: 一只股票可能开盘就猛拉，在那个位置横一两个小时，到收盘时基本又回落、向均值回归，对吧？

turns.en: A little bit higher than started, but lower than the day's high. And so a lot of traders have said to us, like, well, wouldn't it be great to just capture that little chunk of time where that stock is really moving?
turns.zh: 收盘时只比起点稍高一点，但远低于当天高点。所以很多交易员跟我们说：要是能只抓住股价真正在动的那一小段时间，该多好啊？

turns.en: And so that's what made us think about this and it's just supposed to be a tool size to match that one hour window, like cleaner, more precise exposure for what traders might want around high conviction for that day, news event, whatever it is that happens that day.
turns.zh: 这正是引发我们思考这个产品的起点。它本就该是一个贴合一个小时窗口的工具——为交易员当天高确信度的判断、新闻事件、或者那天发生的任何事，提供更干净、更精准的敞口。

turns.en: How exactly do you go about structuring a product? I mean, I'm not gonna go too into the weeds because this could be a master's thesis on how kind of derivative instruments and market structure and market making works, but you're talking about a product that is very sophisticated that you have to risk manage on literally an hour to hour basis during the course of any given day.
turns.zh: 你们到底是怎么搭建一个产品结构的？我不想钻太深，因为讲衍生品、市场结构和做市机制就够写一整篇硕士论文了。但你说的是一个极其精密的产品，在一天之中真的要逐小时做风险管理。

turns.en: How exactly do you kind of yet or construct ETFs like that? Is it to say that these ETFs have a shelf life and they kind of just disappear at some point or are they kind of resetting and then going back to a certain level and then resetting for the next hour?
turns.zh: 这样的ETF你们到底怎么构建？是不是说这些ETF有一个保质期，到某个时点就消失了？还是说它们重置之后回到某个水平，然后为下一个小时再重置？

turns.en: How exactly do we potentially see these things evolving? Is it a ticker that changes rapidly during the course of any given day and it does it for days, weeks and months at a time?
turns.zh: 这些产品未来可能会怎么演化？是一个在一天之内快速变动的代码，日复一日、周复一周、月复一月地持续下去？

turns.en: Or are we talking about ETFs that may have a shelf life and then kind of disappear only for another one to take its place? So the thing that's great about this is they work basically the same way that the daily 2X funds work.
turns.zh: 还是说这些ETF可能有保质期，到期消失，然后另一只接着顶上来？这个产品的妙处在于，它运作起来和每日2倍基金基本是一样的。

turns.en: And in a lot of cases, you're using a total return swap, right? And at the end of the day, the market or the index that you're tracking or the single stock that you're tracking closes.
turns.zh: 很多时候你用的是总收益互换（total return swap），对吧？到一天结束时，你跟踪的市场、指数或单只股票收盘结算。

turns.en: And if it's closed up 2% and you have a 2X daily funds, then you're looking for that 4% of exposure. And so the ETF issuer in that case would buy exposure on the swap so that when you're rebalancing the nav, it's showing that 2X that you got for the day.
turns.zh: 如果它收盘涨了2%，而你持有的是一只2倍每日基金，那你要的就是4%的敞口。这种情况下，ETF发行商就会在互换上买入敞口，这样当你再平衡净值（NAV）时，呈现的就是你当天应得的那2倍。

turns.en: And this just happens basically at the end of each hour. So it's through the use of equity derivatives, total return swaps, it can be done with options.
turns.zh: 小时级产品基本上就是把这件事挪到每个小时结束时做一次。它通过股票衍生品、总收益互换来实现，也可以用期权来做。

turns.en: And it's really the same thing. So for every $2 of performance, you basically get times two, 200%, you get $4 of return. And this can obviously work the other way too.
turns.zh: 本质上是一回事：底层每2美元的涨幅，你拿到两倍、也就是200%，变成4美元的回报。当然，反方向也同样适用。

turns.en: So if the market is down throughout the day and we're resetting every hour, you can think about like, well, how does that look versus a end of day ETF, right?
turns.zh: 所以如果市场全天都在下跌，而我们每小时重置一次，你可以想想：跟一只收盘才重置的ETF比起来，表现会是什么样？

turns.en: That didn't reduce its exposure every hour throughout the day. So even on the downside, if you're trending downwards, we're taking exposure off the table every hour, right?
turns.zh: 后者不会在一天中每小时削减敞口。所以即便在下跌方向，只要趋势向下，我们也是每小时把一部分敞口撤下来。

turns.en: So the performance comparisons will be interesting to see and with volatile markets, both of those will do poorly. If you have a 2X CTF that rebalances at the end of the day, you hold it for a couple of days and there's range around volatility, you're probably gonna do worse than 2X, right?
turns.zh: 所以两者的业绩对比会很有意思，而在震荡市场里两者都会表现不佳。如果你持有一只收盘再平衡的2倍ETF，拿上几天、市场又是区间震荡，你大概率会跑输2倍，对吧？

turns.en: And then same thing with the hourly reset during that time period, you'll do worse than 2X. So, but it works the same way. That's the same way that the levered funds that were used to work.
turns.zh: 同样，小时级重置产品在那种时段里也会跑输2倍。但机制是一样的，和已有杠杆基金的运作方式完全相同。

turns.en: It's just a reset at the end of the hour. All right, so there are products, as we all know, that are in the market right now and are resetting on that daily basis for 2X exposure to any kind of product.
turns.zh: 只是重置改在了每小时结束。好，我们都知道，现在市场上已经有每日重置、为各类产品提供2倍敞口的基金了。

turns.en: How much do you think about, first of all, we should also say, as of this podcast taping, these products are not live. You have applied- No, they're not live.
turns.zh: 你们思考的程度如何——首先我们得说明，截至本期节目录制时，这些产品还没有上线。你们只是提交了申请——对，还没有上线。

turns.en: Right, you have applied- Right, exactly, not live, not effective, but you have put them out there in the kind of, I guess under the assumption that they could be live and or effective at some point in the not so distant future.
turns.zh: 对，你们提交了申请——是的，没上线、没生效，但你们还是把它们推出来了，我想是默认在不太远的将来某个时点它们会上线或生效。

turns.en: How much do you kind of put on both your product development hat, because that's what you do, but then also your regulator hat for what you think the kind of concerns and or maybe issues would be from bringing these to product, these products to market from a regulatory standpoint.
turns.zh: 你们既戴上产品开发这顶帽子——因为这是你们的本职——也戴上监管视角的帽子，从监管层面看，把这些产品推向市场会有哪些担忧和问题？

turns.en: Yeah, I mean, I think our, so from a product perspective, we thought that these products were in line with the 2X daily resetting ETFs, where we understand what the maximum, the current maximum permitted leverage is out there through, you know, the derivatives rule and ATF4 and the information is out there.
turns.zh: 嗯，从产品角度看，我们认为这些产品与2倍每日重置ETF是同一路径的。现行衍生品规则和ATF4框架下允许的最大杠杆是多少，这些信息都是公开的，我们心里有数。

turns.en: So it's a 2X product, it's in line with the 2X products that already exist. You know, the difference is the hourly frequency, it's, you know, to our knowledge, there isn't a limit on how many times you can rebalance the fund throughout the day.
turns.zh: 所以它是2倍产品，和已有的2倍产品一脉相承。区别只在小时级的频率。据我们所知，监管并没有规定一天里最多能再平衡多少次。

turns.en: But, you know, ultimately it's, it'll be, you know, kind of up to the regulator to give feedback, ask questions and of course we cooperate and collaborate and, you know, ensure we're doing that.
turns.zh: 但最终还是要看监管给反馈、提问题，我们当然会配合、会协作，确保做到这些。

turns.en: But we felt strongly that this was a product that is viable for the marketplace and fits into the construct of levered number of CTFs that are already out there.
turns.zh: 但我们强烈认为，这是一个在市场上立得住的产品，契合当前已经存在的这一批杠杆ETF的整体框架。

turns.en: And then, you know, how do we think about it? Like the biggest thing for us is just making sure the education is out there, making sure that, you know, the correct investors are using it and investors understand the risks and the benefits associated with these products.
turns.zh: 那我们是怎么考虑这个问题的？对我们来说，最重要的就是确保教育内容到位，确保正确的投资者在使用它，确保投资者理解这些产品伴随的风险和收益。

turns.en: So our mindset of an ETF issuer is exactly the same, right? Just make sure we explain how they work fairly, educate, you know, as much as possible.
turns.zh: 我们作为ETF发行商的心态完全一样：确保公允地解释产品如何运作，尽可能把教育做充分。

turns.en: But in terms of running the product, we're obviously very well versed with that. We already do it for the 2X leverage funds. And again, it's not much different to run this.
turns.zh: 至于运作产品本身，我们显然驾轻就熟。2倍杠杆基金我们早就在做，再强调一次，运作这个产品并没有太大不同。

turns.en: So you had brought up the idea of education and just how much the types of people will be using this type of product to kind of gain the outcomes that they want to.
turns.zh: 你刚才提到教育的理念，以及什么样的人会用这类产品去获得他们想要的结果。

turns.en: With my final question for you here, I'd like to ask you a little bit about at what, I guess what types of investors are you trying to target for this type of product?
turns.zh: 最后一个问题想请你聊聊：这类产品你们想瞄准的是哪一类投资者？

turns.en: Is it predominantly a retail investor base that you're kind of looking for here? Are you looking for more hedge fund type clients? And I know that everyone's gonna use these things once they are hypothetically out there, live and in the wild.
turns.zh: 主要面向散户投资者吗？还是说你们更想要对冲基金类型的客户？我知道一旦这些产品真的假设性落地、上线运行，所有人都会去用。

turns.en: But when you conceive the product, was there a certain part of the market that you thought would be more, I guess, open to using these types of intraday reset type products on a levered size?
turns.zh: 但在构思产品时，你们觉得市场的哪个部分会更愿意接受这种杠杆类的盘中重置产品？

turns.en: Yeah, I mean, I think that these are investment vehicles basically for very active, sophisticated investors, whether they're institutional or their retail-like institution.
turns.zh: 我觉得这些投资工具本质上是为非常活跃、成熟的投资者准备的，无论他们是机构，还是像机构一样的散户。

turns.en: It's really interesting because a lot of the times we'll be talking to a retail person and that retail person is a trader at a hedge fund. And there's different types of retail traders, of course, but this is really a tool for active, sophisticated investors looking to gain magnified or inverse exposure to a market.
turns.zh: 很有意思的是，很多时候我们在和一个“散户”交流，结果对方其实是对冲基金的交易员。当然散户交易员也分不同类型，但这个工具确实是给那些想要放大或反向敞口的活跃成熟投资者准备的。

turns.en: They're very well aware of the risks. They're very well aware of the fund's objectives and what leverage means and what amplified exposure means in both trending markets and volatile markets and things like this.
turns.zh: 他们非常清楚风险，非常了解基金的目标、杠杆意味着什么，以及在趋势性市场和震荡市场里放大敞口分别意味着什么。

turns.en: I would just say sophisticated short-term traders looking to trade on short-term intraday market catalysts. All right, well, Sylvia Jablonski, CIO and co-founder of Defines ETFs.
turns.zh: 一句话概括：瞄准盘中短期催化剂的成熟短线交易者。好，感谢你，Sylvia Jablonski，Defiance ETFs 首席投资官兼联合创始人。

turns.en: Thank you so much for taking the time to join us here and please come back and give us the update for when these things progress down the pipeline.
turns.zh: 非常感谢你抽时间做客节目。等这些产品在审批管道里往前推进之后，请一定再回来给我们更新进展。

turns.en: We will, for sure we will do. Thank you. All right, that does it for ETF Edge, the podcast. Thanks for listening. Join us again next week or just head over to etfedge.cnbc.com.
turns.zh: 我们一定会的，谢谢。好的，本期《ETF Edge》播客就到这里。感谢收听。下周再会，或者访问 etfedge.cnbc.com。

turns.en: Over the last few decades, technology has transformed our world in amazing ways. Through it all, Invesco QQQ ETF has connected investors to the forefront of innovation.
turns.zh: 过去几十年，科技以惊人的方式改变了我们的世界。一路走来，Invesco QQQ ETF 始终将投资者与创新的最前沿连接在一起。

turns.en: Access the future today with Invesco QQQ. Let's rethink possibility. There are risks when investing in ETFs, including possible loss of money.
turns.zh: 今天就用 Invesco QQQ 触及未来。让我们重新想象可能性。投资ETF存在风险，包括可能损失本金。

turns.en: ETF risks are similar to those of stocks. Investments in the tech sector are subject to greater risk and more volatility than more diversified investments.
turns.zh: ETF的风险与股票类似。对科技板块的投资比更分散化的投资面临更大的风险和更多的波动。

turns.en: The NASDAQ 100 Index includes the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the NASDAQ. An investment cannot be made directly to an index.
turns.zh: 纳斯达克100指数（NASDAQ-100）包含在纳斯达克上市的100家最大的非金融公司。投资者无法直接投资于指数。

turns.en: Before investing, consider the fund's investment objectives, risks, charges, and expenses. Visit Invesco.com for a prospectus containing this information.
turns.zh: 投资前请考虑基金的投资目标、风险、收费和开支。请访问 Invesco.com 获取包含这些信息的招募说明书。

turns.en: Read it carefully before investing. Invesco Distributors, Inc.
turns.zh: 投资前请仔细阅读。Invesco Distributors, Inc.
